faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.sub: Everything you need to know about Takt Studio and line simulation

items.q: How accurate are Takt Studio's calculations?
items.a: Calculations are based on standard Industrial Organization Engineering formulas. Accuracy depends on the quality of input data (cycle times, efficiencies). It is an analytical simulation tool for decision-making, not a real-time control system.

items.q: Where is my simulation data stored?
items.a: For privacy and security, your data never leaves your device. It is stored in your browser's local storage (localStorage). If you clear your cache or switch browsers, data will not sync unless you export it manually.

items.q: Can I export my analyses to other formats?
items.a: Yes, Takt Studio lets you export results and the current configuration as PDF for presentations and technical reports, as well as import/export JSON files to share models between users.

items.q: Do I need advanced Lean Manufacturing knowledge?
items.a: Not required, but it helps. The tool is designed to be intuitive, but concepts like 'Bottleneck' or 'Line Balancing' are fundamental to correctly interpret results and make improvement decisions.

privacidad.metaDescription: How we handle your data in Takt Studio: local storage, language cookie, Vercel and your GDPR rights.
privacidad.title: Privacy
privacidad.subtitle: Your engineering data is yours. Full transparency about information handling.

cards.title: Privacy by Design
cards.text: We do not store your model data on external servers. All computation happens in your browser.

cards.title: No Accounts
cards.text: No registration required. No user profiles or personal identity tracking.

cards.title: Local Security
cards.text: Data persistence uses your browser's local storage (localStorage).

p: The data controller is Marc Cubero Cantavella, based in Valencia (Spain), owner and developer of Takt Studio.

The contact channel for any privacy matter is the email address taktstudio.app@gmail.com. As an alternative channel, especially for technical issues, the issue tracker (Issues) of the project's public repository on GitHub is also available. Given the personal, non-commercial nature of the project, no data protection officer has been appointed.

sections.t: 2. What data is processed and where it is stored
p: Takt Studio does not collect or receive personally identifiable data. All data you enter into the simulator (station names, cycle times, operators, failure rates, economic parameters, scenarios, snapshots and configuration preferences) is stored exclusively in your browser's local storage (localStorage), on your own device.

This data is never transmitted to the owner or to third parties: all computation happens in your browser. If you share a scenario via link, the configuration travels encoded within the URL itself and is only received by the person you choose to send it to.
You can delete all your data at any time using the reset option in the application itself, or by clearing the site's data in your browser settings.

The application uses a single cookie, NEXT_LOCALE, which remembers your language preference (Spanish or English) for up to one year. It is a strictly necessary cookie to provide the requested service, and is therefore exempt from consent under Article 22.2 of Spanish Law 34/2002 (LSSI-CE).
No advertising, tracking or third-party cookies are used.

To work offline, the application installs a Service Worker that stores temporary copies of pages and assets in your device's cache. This cache contains no information beyond the application itself and your local data, and you can delete it at any time by clearing the site's data in your browser.

The application is served from the Vercel platform (Vercel Inc., United States). When you visit any page, its servers automatically process technical connection data —IP address, user agent, date and time, requested URL— in logs for security, performance and service operation purposes, in accordance with Vercel's privacy policy.
Vercel acts as a data processor and any international data transfers are covered by the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework and/or standard contractual clauses approved by the European Commission.

We use Vercel Analytics and Speed Insights to obtain aggregate usage metrics (page views, referrers) and performance metrics (Web Vitals). These tools do not use cookies, do not collect personally identifiable data and do not build individual profiles: all information is anonymous and aggregated.
Since no cookies or personal identifiers are used, this analytics setup does not require a consent banner.

The legal basis for processing technical connection data and aggregate analytics is legitimate interest (Art. 6.1.f GDPR) in operating, protecting and improving the application. Your simulation data is not processed by the owner, as it never leaves your device.

You have the rights of access, rectification, erasure, objection, restriction of processing and portability (Arts. 15 to 22 GDPR). In practice, since your simulation data resides solely on your device, you can exercise most of these rights directly by deleting it from your browser.

For any request or inquiry you can open an issue in the project's repository on GitHub. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency (www.aepd.es) if you believe the processing does not comply with the regulations.

The application links to third-party sites (GitHub, LinkedIn, Universidad Europea de Valencia and Porcelanosa) which have their own privacy policies. The owner is not responsible for the data processing practices of those sites.

This policy may be updated to reflect changes in the application or in the law. The current version, with its last-updated date, will always be available on this page, and significant changes will be announced in the project's repository.

metodologia.title: Methodology and model assumptions
metodologia.subtitle: How Takt Studio calculates its metrics and the limitations of the analytical model.
metodologia.introP1: Takt Studio is a deterministic analytical model of industrialized production lines. It uses cycle times, number of operators, demand and shifts to calculate key operational metrics: takt time, throughput, lead time and balancing efficiency.
metodologia.introP2: The tool is neither a full discrete event simulation (DES) nor a definitive financial validation. Its value lies in pre-validating improvement decisions before intervening on the shop floor, providing a fast and rigorous first quantitative approximation.
metodologia.introWarning: The results are indicative. For real investment decisions, they should be calibrated with actual line operational and financial data.

playground.title: ⚡ Interactive Mini-Lab: Real-time Takt Time
playground.subtitle: Adjust the parameters to observe how the required production pace changes instantly.

kpiCards.title: Takt Time
kpiCards.p: Pace at which to produce to meet demand. Expresses the maximum allowed time per unit.
kpiCards.note: A low takt time indicates aggressive demand; a high takt time, relaxed demand.

kpiCards.title: Effective cycle time
kpiCards.p: Actual time consumed by a station per unit, considering parallel operators and rework rate.
kpiCards.note: More operators reduce effective time; more failures increase it due to inherent rework.

kpiCards.title: Bottleneck
kpiCards.p: Station that limits the overall pace of the line: the one with the highest effective cycle time.
kpiCards.note: Alleviating the bottleneck is the action with the highest impact on overall throughput.

kpiCards.title: Throughput
kpiCards.p: Maximum units the line can produce per day, limited by the bottleneck.
kpiCards.note: Throughput never exceeds the bottleneck's capacity, regardless of other stations' performance.

kpiCards.title: Lead Time
kpiCards.p: Estimated total time it takes for a unit to travel the entire line from input to output.
kpiCards.note: Does not model queues or buffer waits; it is an approximation of pure travel time.

kpiCards.title: Balancing efficiency
kpiCards.p: Measure of how balanced the effective times are across stations.
kpiCards.note: A value of 1.0 indicates a perfectly balanced line. Values below 0.7 suggest an opportunity to redistribute workloads.

metodologia.econIntro: Takt Studio's economic layer translates operational metrics into financial impact estimates under scenario-configurable assumptions.
metodologia.proxyText: The difference between the contribution generated by served units and the total daily operating cost.
metodologia.impactText: For each proposed improvement action, the estimated change in contribution minus the change in operating costs is calculated.
metodologia.paybackText: If the recommendation involves a one-off initial investment (method or quality improvement), the recovery time is estimated.
metodologia.econWarning: The economic layer is an indicative estimate under configurable assumptions. It does not replace a detailed financial analysis or the company's real accounting validation.
metodologia.stochasticIntro: To complement the real-time deterministic calculation, Takt Studio incorporates a Monte Carlo simulation engine with 2,000 stochastic runs and a parameter sensitivity laboratory.
metodologia.mcText: Each line station simulates random cycle time variability following a truncated normal distribution computed via the Box-Muller transform and the Mulberry32 PRNG generator.
metodologia.mcPercentiles: From 2,000 runs, the P10 (conservative scenario), P50 (expected median), and P90 (optimistic scenario) percentiles are extracted, providing a probabilistic Throughput risk matrix.
metodologia.sensitivityText: Projects line performance across continuous demand sweeps (±50%) and labor variations, visually highlighting the inflection points where the line enters deficit.

limits.label: Deterministic / Stochastic Duality
limits.text: The core model provides real-time deterministic calculation (<1 ms). For plant variability and risk analysis, the 2,000-run Monte Carlo stochastic engine is deployed.

limits.label: No full DES
limits.text: It is not a discrete event simulation (DES). It does not model queues, buffers or WIP accumulation between stations.

limits.label: No complex sequencing
limits.text: It does not model alternative routings, complex parallelism or sequence dependencies between stations.

limits.label: Approximate bottleneck
limits.text: The bottleneck is identified as the station with the highest effective cycle time. In reality, the constraint may also depend on WIP policies, staggered shifts or materials.

limits.label: Indicative economic layer
limits.text: Costs, margins and impacts are configurable estimates. They must be calibrated with real accounting and operational data before being used for investment decisions.

limits.label: Simplified lead time
limits.text: Lead time is the sum of effective times. It does not include queue waiting times or transport times between stations.

metodologia.noteP1: Takt Studio's value lies in offering a fast and consistent first quantitative approximation to pre-validate improvement decisions before intervening on the real line. It allows discarding unviable options, prioritizing interventions with the greatest operational impact and backing proposals with numbers.
metodologia.noteP2: For real investment, plant reorganization or hiring decisions, Takt Studio results should be complemented with:
noteItems: In-situ operational validation (direct observation, time studies)
Detailed financial analysis with real accounting data
DES simulation if line complexity justifies it
Judgment of the engineering team and production management

templates.title: Industrial Templates Guide
templates.subtitle: Detailed technical data sheets for the 7 predefined sectors in Takt Studio. Analyze the base configuration, cycle times, and typical challenges of each industry.

descriptions.monobath: Flagship template based on industrialized modular construction. It features high manual dependency, variable bottlenecks, and significant failure rates in the waterproofing and tiling phases, making it ideal for experimenting with Monte Carlo simulation.
descriptions.automotive: Highly balanced production line where Takt Time is strict. The bottleneck is usually found in the powertrain marriage, and variability is low, prioritizing continuous flow and automation.
descriptions.electronics: Process characterized by very short cycle times and high automation (Pick & Place). Performance constraints usually stem from baking times or optical inspection (AOI), where flow slows down.
descriptions.logistics: Environment with high human variability. Picking and packing rely heavily on operator fatigue and order complexity, showing very pronounced lognormal distributions in real times.
descriptions.ceramics: Capital-intensive continuous process industry. The bottleneck is rigidly set at the roller kiln and the hydraulic press. Efficiency depends on minimizing downtime at these critical stations.
descriptions.food_pharma: Sector subject to strict hygienic regulations. It features scheduled cleaning stops (C.I.P.) and the bottleneck is usually in the sterilization phase (autoclave) or packaging sealing.
descriptions.machinery: Make-to-Order or low-volume production. Long cycle times (measured in hours or days), high need for skilled labor, and high probability of reworks due to the complexity of pressure and quality testing.

tutorial.title: Step-by-Step Tutorial
tutorial.subtitle: Learn to simulate, diagnose, and optimize your industrial production line in 6 sequential steps.

s1.title: Base Configuration
s1.desc: Define the daily demand volume required by the client and configure the effective hours of your workday.
s1.theory: The Takt Time is the heartbeat of the customer. It represents the pace at which you must manufacture a product to meet demand. Any station taking longer than this time will be a Bottleneck.
s1.tip: Do not use a full 8-hour shift. Subtract breaks, preventive maintenance, and meetings (OEE - Availability). Use real values (e.g., 7.2 hours).
s1.action: Go to the top-left panel and adjust the 'Daily Demand' and 'Shift Hours'. You will see the Takt Time recalculate instantly.

s2.title: Station Modeling
s2.desc: Build your line by adding each station. Enter the timed cycle time, the number of assigned operators, and the failure rate.
s2.theory: The 'Cycle Time' (CT) is the actual time it takes a station to complete its task. The 'Failure Rate' introduces the probability of rework or scrap, which is vital for stochastic models.
s2.tip: Avoid ideal times. Use direct time studies on the shop floor with rating techniques, and add an allowance for human fatigue (usually 10-15%).
s2.action: In the central area, click 'Add Station'. Use the sliders to configure the time and watch how the capacity bar fills up against the Takt Time.

s3.title: Constraint Diagnostics
s3.desc: The simulator will instantly identify the Bottleneck (the slowest station) and calculate the theoretical maximum Throughput.
s3.theory: The Theory of Constraints (TOC) indicates that the total performance of the system is dictated solely and exclusively by the Bottleneck. Improving a non-bottleneck station is a mirage.
s3.tip: If your Bottleneck exceeds the Takt Time, the line will not be able to meet demand without overtime. Your first improvement goal must be this station.
s3.action: Look for the station marked in dark red in the bar chart. The top KPI panel will show you the 'Line Balancing Efficiency'.

s4.title: Sensitivity Analysis (Monte Carlo)
s4.desc: Start the stochastic simulation. The system will run thousands of iterations applying variability to show you the real behavior of the line under uncertainty.
s4.theory: In real life, times are not fixed (deterministic). They follow a lognormal distribution. The Monte Carlo method reveals hidden risk by calculating the P90 percentile (the worst probable scenario).
s4.tip: If the P50 (median) meets the demand, but the P90 does not, your line is fragile. A minor breakdown will cause severe delivery delays.
s4.action: Click the 'Run Monte Carlo' button in the KPI panel. Observe how the bottom graph changes to a bell curve (Histogram) with percentiles.

s5.title: Economic Modeling
s5.desc: Define the operating costs of your plant. Set the labor cost per hour and the hourly cost of having the line stopped due to the Bottleneck.
s5.theory: In industrial engineering, time is money. The Downtime Cost of the slowest station defines the financial viability of any investment. If your bottleneck stops the line for 1 hour, you lose the contribution margin of that entire hour.
s5.tip: Be realistic with the Labor Cost: include social charges and taxes, not just the base salary. Use Fully Burdened costs.
s5.action: In the Configuration panel, go to the 'Economics' section. Adjust the hourly operator cost and the hourly downtime cost of the bottleneck.

s6.title: What-If Comparison
s6.desc: Save the baseline scenario and create a copy. Test changes (e.g., adding an operator) and use the A/B comparator to see the numerical impact.
s6.theory: Line Balancing seeks to match the cycle times of all stations to the Takt Time. This reduces 'Idle Time' and maximizes the Contribution Margin.
s6.tip: Before spending money on robots (CAPEX), try to level the load by moving tasks from the slowest station to the fastest ones.
s6.action: In the top right, save a 'Snapshot'. Then make your changes, and go to the 'Comparator' tab to see the cost and efficiency deltas (Δ) side by side.

s7.title: Executive Reporting
s7.desc: Once the improvement is validated, export the full analysis to a vector PDF report, ready to justify your investment proposal.
s7.theory: Top management requires financial metrics. Translating 'Efficiency' to 'Euros Saved by Rework' is key to getting continuous improvement projects approved.
s7.tip: Use the 'ROI Calculator' in the report to demonstrate Payback. A 5% increase in efficiency usually pays for the investment in less than 3 months.
s7.action: In the top bar, click the PDF Export icon. An A4 corporate document will be generated with all mathematical graphs and tables.
